items.issue: The training band 'tc' is described as 'Tilt angle or total curvature - magnetic field derivative for edge detection', but it is rank-identical (Spearman 1.0000, n=299,822) to the GeoDAWN radiometric total-count grid and only -0.15 correlated with the magnetic horizontal gradient (tmi_hg). Verified this session from the pinned rasters.
items.action: Do not use 'tc' as a magnetic edge transform; treat it as gamma-ray total count.

items.issue: Berkowitz et al. (2000) give ensemble-average connectivity estimates ('rather than particular realizations'); they do not state that one segment decides whether two particular faults join.
items.action: The per-gap argument here rests on the graph analysis and the holdout, not on the paper alone.

items.issue: The catalogue is 3,199 systems (median 1.27 km; 2,211 shorter than 2 km). Holdout truth is catalogue-internal, so segmentation can inflate link enrichment relative to genuinely new expert-mapped faults.
items.action: Class-level validation only; the live score is the only test of the real hidden set.

items.issue: My first confirmatory launch applied the minimum gap before choosing the nearest target (deviation from the registered rule); caught by a unit test, stopped, disclosed, rerun as registered.
The dotted H19-5 base was trained on all labels, so its coverage of hidden catalogue pieces is inflated and its DTI on the holdout (~0.098) is not comparable to the live 0.2477.
Carried from the sibling record (not re-verified): GeoDAWN metadata has placeholder fields and line-km mismatches (151,799 vs 149,030).
Leaderboard rows smrtdoog5 and SDCF9 are associated with the owner in sibling notes but ownership and compliance with the one-entity / 3-per-week rules are unverified.
items.action: Owner to confirm before relying on additional accounts.

items.issue: The pre-registration texts precede the runs in the working session, but git history (first commit after the runs) cannot prove it; no external timestamp exists.
items.action: Gates are disciplined, not notarised; the live score is the real test. See the 'Provenance limit' section of knowledge/03.

items.issue: An earlier edge builder over-counted loops (cyclomatic number 504, caused by 1-px stubs recorded as self-loops). Corrected in review pass 2: raw 250; 110 after dropping self-loops <= 3 px; only 6 enclosed regions >= 20 px.
items.action: Use the corrected figures (evidence/graph_report.json); the catalogue is nearly acyclic at 100 m.
